papers.claim: Trailing-1d z-score of log(bid/ask depth) at 1/2/5% bands has |IC| <= 0.012 against 4h-24h forward returns on 50 Binance USDT-M perps, and a cross-sectional long/short implementation nets -12 to -15 bps per trade after 14 bps RT plus funding in every year 2023-2026.
papers.decision: Do not promote. Depth imbalance is dominated by costs at 4h-24h. Next wave: (a) fix the h24 harness (align entries on a shared calendar grid, require >=10 names per timestamp, use a block bootstrap with blocks >= horizon instead of non-overlapping subsampling); (b) test depth *change* (delta of log imbalance over 1h/4h) and depth-vs-OI interaction, which were planned but not reached inside the run_code budget; (c) test whether depth imbalance predicts short-horizon (5m-1h) returns, where it may clear a smaller cost bar.
papers.description: Family f14. Built a 5m panel for all 50 symbols from /dataset/discovery/bars_5m joined to depth_5m on avail_ms (closed bars only, tolerance 15 min), 2023-01..2026-04 (depth coverage starts 2023-01 for all 50 symbols). Signal = trailing-1-day z-score of log(bid depth / ask depth) at 1%, 2% and 5% bands. Raw predictive power is tiny: pooled per-symbol Spearman IC vs forward log return is +0.0015 (z1,h4), -0.0037 (z1,h24), +0.0069 (z2,h4), +0.0118 (z5,h4), +0.0068 (z5,h24) with standard errors ~0.0015-0.0023 across 50 symbols. The best raw IC (z5,h4 = 0.0118) implies a gross edge of roughly 1-2 bps per trade at typical 4h return dispersion, an order of magnitude below the 14-19 bps round-trip cost. The cross-sectional long-top-5/short-bottom-5 implementation (non-overlapping entries every h bars, 14 bps RT + funding actually crossed, funding available for 39/50 symbols) returns -12.95 bps/trade at h4 for z1, -13.73 for z2, -13.76 for z5, with hit rates 0.34-0.40 and per-year means between -11.1 and -14.8 bps in every year 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026 (Jan-Apr). The h24 cross-sectional run produced zero evaluable timestamps in this build because the per-symbol stride subsample plus the funding-coverage filter left fewer than 10 symbols per timestamp; that is a harness limitation, not evidence, and is reported as such. Conclusion: depth imbalance is a real but sub-cost microstructure signal at these horizons; it cannot pay 14-19 bps round trip. Filed as a clean negative.
papers.kill_criterion: Kill permanently if a wave-2 rerun on a shared entry grid still shows |IC| < 0.02 at h4-h24 or a cross-sectional net below 0 bps/trade at 14 bps RT in any two of the years 2023-2026.
papers.limitations: Depth coverage starts 2023-01 so no 2020-2022 walk-forward years exist for this family; only 39/50 symbols have funding so the cross-section is thinned; depth_5m is a 5-minute snapshot, not a time-weighted book; no bid/ask spread measurement, so queue/spread effects are modelled as a flat 14 bps; universe is survivorship-biased to the 50 symbols listed in 2026; the h24 cross-sectional run returned zero evaluable timestamps (harness bug, reported in the method record); the 200-shuffled-day placebo was not run because no variant reached the candidate stage.

metrics.cost_model: 14 bps round trip + funding actually crossed (39/50 symbols have funding); the 19 bps-for-all case would be 5 bps worse
metrics.decay: flat negative across 2023-2026, no decay to detect
metrics.placebo_max: not run (no candidate reached the placebo stage)

# f14 depth-imbalance sanity + cross-sectional test (numpy/pandas only, /dataset paths)
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, glob, os
from scipy.stats import spearmanr
SYMS=sorted(os.listdir("/dataset/discovery/depth_5m"))
def load(tab,s):
    fs=sorted(glob.glob(f"/dataset/discovery/{tab}/{s}/*.parquet"))
    return pd.concat([pd.read_parquet(f) for f in fs],ignore_index=True) if fs else None
def zs(x,win=288):
    s=pd.Series(x); m=s.rolling(win,min_periods=win//2).mean(); sd=s.rolling(win,min_periods=win//2).std()
    return ((s-m)/sd).values
# 1) per-symbol panel: 5m bars joined to depth on avail_ms (closed bars only)
for s in SYMS:
    b=load("bars_5m",s)[["ts_ms","close"]].sort_values("ts_ms")
    d=load("depth_5m",s).sort_values("ts_ms")
    b["close_ms"]=b["ts_ms"]+300_000
    m=pd.merge_asof(b.sort_values("close_ms"),
        d[["avail_ms","depth_bid_1pct_usd","depth_ask_1pct_usd","depth_bid_2pct_usd",
           "depth_ask_2pct_usd","depth_bid_5pct_usd","depth_ask_5pct_usd"]].sort_values("avail_ms"),
        left_on="close_ms",right_on="avail_ms",direction="backward",tolerance=900_000)
    lp=np.log(m["close"].values.astype(float)); n=len(m)
    o=pd.DataFrame({"ts_ms":m["ts_ms"].values})
    for h in (4,8,12,24):
        k=h*12; f=np.full(n,np.nan); f[:n-k]=lp[k:]-lp[:n-k]; o[f"f{h}"]=f
    for p in (1,2,5):
        li=np.log(m[f"depth_bid_{p}pct_usd"].values.astype(float)/m[f"depth_ask_{p}pct_usd"].values.astype(float))
        o[f"li{p}"]=li; o[f"z{p}"]=zs(li)
    o.to_parquet(f"/work/sigsym/{s}.parquet",index=False)
# 2) pooled per-symbol Spearman IC of trailing-1d z(log bid/ask depth) vs forward return
for p in (1,2,5):
    for h in (4,8,12,24):
        ics=[]
        for s in SYMS:
            d=pd.read_parquet(f"/work/sigsym/{s}.parquet",columns=[f"z{p}",f"f{h}"]).dropna().iloc[::7]
            if len(d)>500: ics.append(spearmanr(d[f"z{p}"],d[f"f{h}"]).statistic)
        print(f"z{p} h{h} IC={np.mean(ics):+.4f} se={np.std(ics)/np.sqrt(len(ics)):.4f} n_sym={len(ics)}")
# 3) cross-sectional long/short: rank z per timestamp, long top5 / short bottom5, non-overlapping
#    entries every h bars, cost 14 bps RT + funding actually crossed (sum of rates in (t0,t1] * side)
FUND={}
for s in SYMS:
    f=load("funding",s)
    FUND[s]=None if f is None else (f.sort_values("ts_ms")["ts_ms"].values.astype(np.int64),
                                    f.sort_values("ts_ms")["rate"].values.astype(float))
def fcost(s,t0,t1,side):
    if FUND.get(s) is None: return np.nan
    ts,r=FUND[s]; i=np.searchsorted(ts,t0,side="right"); j=np.searchsorted(ts,t1,side="right")
    return 0.0 if j<=i else float(r[i:j].sum())*side
for sig in ("z1","z2","z5"):
    for h in (4,24):
        parts=[]
        for s in SYMS:
            d=pd.read_parquet(f"/work/sigsym/{s}.parquet").sort_values("ts_ms").reset_index(drop=True)
            d["sig"]=d[sig]; d=d.iloc[::h*12].dropna(subset=["sig",f"f{h}"])
            parts.append(d[["ts_ms","sig",f"f{h}"]].assign(sym=s))
        df=pd.concat(parts,ignore_index=True)
        df["year"]=pd.to_datetime(df["ts_ms"],unit="ms").dt.year
        rows=[]
        for ts,g in df.groupby("ts_ms"):
            if len(g)<10: continue
            g=g.sort_values("sig"); k=min(5,len(g)//4)
            t0=int(ts); t1=t0+h*3600_000; pnl=0.0; n=0
            for _,r in g.iloc[-k:].iterrows():
                fc=fcost(r["sym"],t0,t1,1)
                if np.isnan(fc): continue
                pnl+=r[f"f{h}"]*1e4-14-fc*1e4; n+=1
            for _,r in g.iloc[:k].iterrows():
                fc=fcost(r["sym"],t0,t1,-1)
                if np.isnan(fc): continue
                pnl+=-r[f"f{h}"]*1e4-14-fc*1e4; n+=1
            if n: rows.append((ts,g["year"].iloc[0],pnl/n))
        r=pd.DataFrame(rows,columns=["ts","year","net"])
        print(sig,h,"net_bps",round(r["net"].mean(),2),"n",len(r))
        print(r.groupby("year")["net"].agg(["mean","count"]).round(2))

            d=pd.read_parquet(f"/work/sigsym/{s}.parquet",columns=[f"z{p}",f"f{h}"]).dropna().iloc[::7]
            if len(d)>500: ics.append(spearmanr(d[f"z{p}"],d[f"f{h}"]).statistic)
        print(f"z{p} h{h} IC={np.mean(ics):+.4f} se={np.std(ics)/np.sqrt(len(ics)):.4f} n_sym={len(ics)}")
FUND={}
for s in SYMS:
    f=load("funding",s)
    FUND[s]=None if f is None else (f.sort_values("ts_ms")["ts_ms"].values.astype(np.int64),
                                    f.sort_values("ts_ms")["rate"].values.astype(float))
def fcost(s,t0,t1,side):

    ts,r=FUND[s]; i=np.searchsorted(ts,t0,side="right"); j=np.searchsorted(ts,t1,side="right")
    return 0.0 if j<=i else float(r[i:j].sum())*side

        rows=[]

                if np.isnan(fc): continue

            for _,r in g.iloc[:k].iterrows():

            if n: rows.append((ts,g["year"].iloc[0],pnl/n))
        r=pd.DataFrame(rows,columns=["ts","year","net"])

        print(r.groupby("year")["net"].agg(["mean","count"]).round(2))

papers.decision: Wave 2 should build the cross-sectional panel on a shared entry grid (bucket = ts_ms // (h*3600_000)) and assert names-per-timestamp >= 10 before evaluating, so an empty result can never be mistaken for a negative.
papers.description: A harness pitfall found while running family f14 and worth broadcasting to the swarm. The natural way to avoid overlapping holds is to take every h-th 5m bar per symbol (iloc[::h*12]). Because each symbol's 5m grid starts at its own listing month and depth coverage starts 2023-01, the resulting timestamps are NOT aligned across symbols: after the subsample the maximum number of symbols sharing a timestamp was 7 (mean 1.86) for h24, so any cross-sectional rule that requires >=10 names per timestamp silently produced zero rows. Combined with a funding-coverage filter (39/50 symbols) the h24 cross-sectional result was empty rather than negative. Fix: align entries on a common calendar grid (e.g. floor(ts_ms / (h*3600_000)) as the entry bucket) instead of per-symbol stride subsampling, and treat missing funding as 'exclude the symbol from that timestamp' rather than 'drop the timestamp'. This cost several run_code calls to diagnose and is the main reason family f14 filed at 18/40 trials.
papers.evidence: Diagnostic: for h24, groupby(ts_ms).size() over the per-symbol stride subsample gave count mean 1.86, max 7, and 0 timestamps with >=10 symbols, so the evaluator emitted no rows. The h4 runs, which use a denser grid, did produce 7014 evaluable timestamps.
papers.title: Method note: per-symbol stride subsampling plus a funding-coverage filter silently empties the h24 cross-section

import numpy as np, pandas as pd
# bars_5m columns: ts_ms, volume, quote_volume, buy/sell_vol, buy/sell_usd, signed_usd,
# n_agg, n_raw, n_buy_agg, large/xlarge buy/sell_usd, n_large, rv_tick, open, high, low, close,
# max_trade_usd, has_trades, n_minutes ; funding: ts_ms, interval_h, rate
COST_RT = 14e-4  # 14 bps round trip (also tested 19 bps)
H = {'h1': 12, 'h4': 48, 'h8': 96, 'h12': 144, 'h24': 288}  # 5m bars

def fwd(o, h):
    # open of bar i+1 -> open of bar i+1+h  (no look-ahead)
    f = np.full(len(o), np.nan)
    f[:-h-1] = np.log(o[h+1:] / o[1:-h])
    return f

def funding_in_window(f_ts, f_rate, t0, t1):
    m = (f_ts >= t0) & (f_ts < t1)
    return float(f_rate[m].sum())

def backtest(o, ts, f_ts, f_rate, signal, h, cost=COST_RT):
    # signal: +1 long, -1 short, 0 flat, decided at close of bar i (uses info <= i)
    f = fwd(o, h)
    pnl, i, n = [], 0, len(o)
    while i < n - h - 1:
        s = signal[i]
        if s == 0 or not np.isfinite(f[i]):
            i += 1; continue
        t0, t1 = ts[i+1], ts[i+1+h]
        fund = funding_in_window(f_ts, f_rate, t0, t1)
        pnl.append(s * f[i] - cost - s * fund)
        i += h + 1  # non-overlapping
    return np.array(pnl)

def placebo_max(pnl, day_id, n_shuf=200, seed=0):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    days = np.unique(day_id)
    obs = pnl.mean()
    mx = -np.inf
    for _ in range(n_shuf):
        perm = rng.permutation(days)
        mp = dict(zip(days, perm))
        sh = pnl[np.argsort([mp[d] for d in day_id])]
        mx = max(mx, sh.mean())
    return obs, mx

# --- seasonality signal builders (all use only calendar info of bar i) ---
def hour_signal(ts, lo, hi):
    hr = ((ts // 3_600_000) % 24).astype(int)
    return np.where((hr >= lo) & (hr < hi), 1, 0)

def dow_signal(ts, dows):
    d = ((ts // 86_400_000) + 4) % 7  # 1970-01-01 was Thursday
    return np.where(np.isin(d, dows), 1, 0)

# Reported results (net bps per trade, 14 bps RT, discovery split, walk-forward by year):
RESULTS = {
  'long 21-22 UTC h4':      -6.05,
  'short 23-24 UTC h1':    -11.78,
  'long 00-00:30 UTC h1':  -10.43,
  'short weekend h24':     -14.20,
  'long weekdays h24':     -16.42,
}
GROSS = {'long 21-22 UTC h4 (gross)': 8.45}
papers.description: Pre-registered negative result for family f17 (time-of-day / day-of-week seasonality). Using 5m bars for 50 Binance USDT-M perpetuals (2020-01 to 2026-04, discovery split only; 3 lockbox windows dropped), we tested unconditional calendar seasonality signals at 4h, 8h, 12h and 24h holding horizons with entry at the open of bar t+1 (no look-ahead), non-overlapping greedy position sizing, 14 bps (and 19 bps) round-trip cost plus realised funding over the holding window, walk-forward evaluation by calendar year, and a 200-shuffle day-permutation placebo to obtain a max-statistic null. Every unconditional seasonality variant failed: long 21:00-22:00 UTC at h=4 net -6.05 bps (held-out -7.56); short 23:00-24:00 UTC pre-settlement at h=1 net -11.78 bps; long 00:00-00:30 UTC post-settlement at h=1 net -10.43 bps; short weekend at h=24 net -14.20 bps; long weekdays at h=24 net -16.42 bps. The best gross (zero-cost) hour-of-day slot, long 21:00-22:00 UTC at h=4, earned only +8.45 bps gross and was sign-unstable across years (negative in 2022 and 2025), i.e. below the 0.12 effect-size floor for train horizons and far below the 200-shuffle placebo maximum. Conclusion: raw intraday/weekly calendar effects in this universe are of order a few bps gross, are dominated by the 14-19 bps round-trip cost, and do not survive the placebo max or the per-year stability requirement. No signal in this family is filed as tradable.
papers.title: Time-of-day and week seasonality in Binance USDT-M perpetuals is not net-of-cost tradable at 4h-24h horizons

import numpy as np

def fwd(o, h):
    f = np.full(len(o), np.nan)
    f[:-h-1] = np.log(o[h+1:] / o[1:-h])
    return f

def pastret(R, k):
    # R[i] = log(o[i+1+h]/o[i+1]); correct lagged k-bar return ending at open of i+1
    P = np.full_like(R, np.nan)
    P[:, k:] = R[:, :-k] - R[:, k:]
    return P

def xs_backtest(R, P, h, cost=14e-4, top_frac=0.2):
    # R: (n_sym, n_t) forward returns; P: (n_sym, n_t) lagged signal
    n_sym, n_t = R.shape
    k = max(1, int(round(n_sym * top_frac)))
    pnl, t = [], 0
    while t < n_t - h - 1:
        col = P[:, t]
        if not np.isfinite(col).all():
            t += 1; continue
        order = np.argsort(col)
        w = np.zeros(n_sym)
        w[order[-k:]] = 1.0 / k     # long winners
        w[order[:k]] = -1.0 / k     # short losers
        pnl.append(float(np.nansum(w * R[:, t])) - cost)
        t += h + 1
    return np.array(pnl)

# Reported (net bps/trade, h=4, cost 14 bps, corrected pastret):
MOM = {6: -106, 12: -144, 24: -198, 48: -279, 144: -275}
REV = {6: 78, 12: 116, 24: 170, 48: 251}
papers.description: Companion study to f17-001 within family f17. We built a vectorised cross-sectional engine over the same 50 USDT-M perpetuals and 5m grid: forward returns are open(t+1)->open(t+1+h) so signals are strictly lagged; past returns are constructed as differences of overlapping forward-return series, P[k] = R[:, :-k] - R[:, k:], which is the algebraically correct lagged return (an earlier naive construction P[:, k:] = R[:, :-k] was found to be misaligned and produced spuriously large positives; all numbers below use the corrected form). With 14 bps round-trip cost, h=4 holding and non-overlapping greedy sizing, cross-sectional momentum is negative at every lookback tested (k=6 bars -106 bps, k=12 -144, k=24 -198, k=48 -279, k=144 -275) while cross-sectional reversal is positive at every lookback (+78, +116, +170, +251 bps respectively). The reversal sign is therefore the only economically coherent gross effect we found, but it is a high-turnover effect whose per-trade edge is concentrated in a small number of days and names, and it did not clear the 200-shuffle day-permutation placebo maximum together with the per-year stability requirement at the 0.12 (train) / 0.35 (held-out h24) effect-size floors. We file it as background rather than useful: the direction is real in-sample but the magnitude is not separable from turnover-driven noise under the pre-registered decision rule. Caveat recorded for the record: the corrected past-return alignment was re-verified against raw BTCUSDT opens (R[p-12] == log(o[i+37]/o[i-11]) confirmed exactly) but the final end-to-end re-run of the reversal variant was cut off by the task budget, so the reversal numbers above should be treated as provisional.
papers.title: Cross-sectional momentum/reversal at 4h-24h on Binance perps: reversal is the only positive gross effect and it does not clear cost plus placebo

papers.description: Audit record for the f17 worker run, filed so the negative results in f17-001 and f17-002 can be interpreted against the number of trials actually spent. Pre-registered budget was 40 trials; the run consumed the budget on the following ledger (net bps per trade at 14 bps round-trip unless marked gross): T1-T5 raw intraday seasonality scans (hour-of-day 5m mean returns, best/worst slots +/-8 to 38 bps, day-of-week means small); T6 long 21-22 UTC h4 -6.05; T7 short pre-settlement 23-24 UTC h1 -11.78; T8 long post-settlement 00-00:30 UTC h1 -10.43; T9 short weekend h24 -14.20; T10 long weekdays h24 -16.42; T11 gross hour-of-day scan, best slot long 21-22 UTC h4 +8.45 gross but sign-unstable by year; T12 cross-sectional hour-of-day momentum h4 +40.27 (later invalidated, see below); T13-T17 cross-sectional momentum/reversal at 4h/24h/7d, all -11 to -16; T18-T22 cross-sectional momentum at 1h/30m/2h/12h, initially +249/+295 but invalidated; T23-T28 corrected cross-sectional momentum/reversal at k=6,12,24,48,144 bars (momentum -106/-144/-198/-279/-275, reversal +78/+116/+170/+251). Two methodological corrections were made mid-run and are disclosed here: (a) the initial past-return construction P[:, k:] = R[:, :-k] was misaligned and produced the spurious large positives in T12 and T18-T22; it was replaced by P[:, k:] = R[:, :-k] - R[:, k:], verified exactly against raw BTCUSDT opens (R[p-12] == log(o[i+37]/o[i-11]) to machine precision); (b) all reported numbers use entry at the open of bar t+1, non-overlapping holds, 14 bps (and 19 bps) round-trip cost, realised funding summed over the holding window, walk-forward by calendar year, and a 200-shuffle day-permutation placebo max. No variant in this family cleared the placebo max together with the effect-size floors (0.12 for train h1/h4, 0.35 for held-out h24) and per-year sign stability, so the family is filed as a clean negative. The run was terminated by the task budget before the final end-to-end re-run of the corrected reversal variant, which is the single open question left for a follow-up worker.

papers.claim: Absorption-style flow-price divergence (high |taker imbalance| with low |price move|, and its mirror: large price move on thin flow) carries no tradable 4h-24h signal on Binance USDT-M perps: per-symbol ICs are |IC| <= 0.014 at 4h and <= 0.005 at 24h, sign-unstable across years and mostly opposite to the hypothesised direction, implying gross edges of a few bps versus 14-19 bps round-trip cost.
papers.decision: Kill the absorption/flow-divergence family in its time-series form. Do not promote to a candidate. Next wave should (a) finish the cross-sectional version (demean forward returns across symbols per 5m bar, rank abs/thin, long-short top/bottom decile, non-overlapping 4h/24h entries, 200 shuffled-day placebos) since that is the only form where a few-bps-per-name edge could aggregate into something above cost, and (b) if that also fails, redirect f07 budget to flow *persistence* (multi-hour imbalance autocorrelation) rather than flow-price divergence.
papers.description: Family f07 (flow-price divergence / absorption). Tested whether taker-flow imbalance that fails to move price (absorption) or price moves on thin flow predict 4h/8h/24h returns on 50 Binance USDT-M perps, 2020-01..2026-04. Signals: fz = z288(signed_usd/quote_volume) (5m taker imbalance, 1-day rolling z), rz = z288(|5m log return|), abs = fz/(1+max(rz,0)) (strong flow, quiet price), thin = fz*max(rz,0) (flow with a big price move). Forward log returns over 48/96/288 five-minute bars. Two evaluation modes: (a) time-series per symbol, (b) cross-sectional (forward return demeaned across symbols per 5m bar, IC per bar averaged). Result: every variant is economically and statistically dead. Time-series ICs are tiny and mostly NEGATIVE (i.e. the opposite sign to the absorption hypothesis): fz->4h IC -0.0050/-0.0042/-0.0036/-0.0034/-0.0007/-0.0043/-0.0023 for 2020..2026; abs->4h -0.0029/-0.0018/-0.0024/-0.0026/+0.0003/-0.0040/-0.0019; thin->4h -0.0103/-0.0141/-0.0063/-0.0068/-0.0063/-0.0006/-0.0018. At 24h all |IC| <= 0.005 and sign-unstable. With per-symbol 5m returns of ~0.3-0.6% std, an IC of 0.005 implies a gross edge of ~2-3 bps per 4h trade, i.e. 5-10x below the 14-19 bps round-trip cost, so no cost model, filter or universe choice can rescue it. The cross-sectional pass (which is the version that could in principle be traded as a dollar-neutral book) was started but the run budget was exhausted before it printed; the time-series evidence alone already fails the MDE floor (0.12 train h1/h4, 0.35 held-out/h24) by more than an order of magnitude, so it is filed as a negative rather than a candidate. No placebo run was warranted: a point estimate that is the wrong sign and 20x below the MDE floor cannot beat the max of 200 shuffled-day placebos.
papers.kill_criterion: Kill if the cross-sectional long-short decile of abs (or thin) has walk-forward net bps/trade <= 0 at 19 bps round trip, or fails to beat the max of 200 shuffled-day placebos, or has |IC| < 0.02 at 4h on the test years.
papers.limitations: 1) Only the time-series (per-symbol) IC pass completed; the cross-sectional dollar-neutral pass was cut off by the run budget, so a cross-sectional absorption effect is not excluded by this record. 2) ICs are pooled per year, not walk-forward-selected parameters, because no parameter survived the first pass to be selected. 3) No placebo was run: the point estimates are the wrong sign and 20x below the MDE floor, so a placebo could not change the verdict. 4) Universe is survivorship-biased (50 symbols listed today). 5) Agg-trade timestamps are first-fill times; no bid/ask, so costs are modelled (14-19 bps) not measured. 6) Funding was not applied because no position was ever held. 7) 2026 covers only Jan-Apr.
papers.title: Flow-price divergence (absorption) at 4h-24h on 50 Binance USDT-M perps: no net-of-cost signal, time-series and cross-sectional

papers.decision: Stop at 9 of 40 trials. The remaining budget is better spent by the next wave on the cross-sectional form and on flow persistence, as stated in the companion negative-result record's decision field.

papers.decision: Adopt fix (1) and (2) in the next wave's protocol: free retries for non-zero-exit run_code calls, and an explicit RAM budget plus a 'stream per symbol, reduce to scalars' recipe in the data section. Also add to the worker prompt: 'if a run_code call fails with an environment error (memory, timeout), change the algorithm, do not resubmit the same script'.
papers.description: In this run a single script was re-submitted many times because it failed on a memory limit (pyarrow ArrowMemoryError on a 19.3M-row float32 frame) rather than on a logic error, and each failed submission consumed one of the 59 run_code calls. The worker prompt says 'at most 59 run_code calls' and the broker blocks at 90% of budget, so a worker that hits an environment limit (RAM, not logic) can burn its entire analysis budget on identical retries and end with no numbers. Two concrete fixes: (1) count only run_code calls that exit 0 toward the analysis budget, or give a separate small retry allowance (e.g. 5 free non-zero-exit calls); (2) put the sandbox RAM limit in the protocol's data section next to the constants, with the recommended pattern for large panels (process one symbol at a time, aggregate to per-year scalars, never concat 50 symbols x 6 years of 5m bars into one frame). Evidence from this run: the SELF_CHECK and the 50-symbol 5m panel build succeeded, the per-symbol IC screen succeeded, and then a pooled 19.3M-row cross-sectional frame failed repeatedly with 'ArrowMemoryError: realloc of size 286601344 failed' until the budget was gone, so the cross-sectional half of the family was never measured.
papers.evidence: SELF_CHECK output: 'CONSTANTS OK 50 symbols; discovery_bytes 8873563632'. Panel build: 50 symbols, 19,275,735 five-minute bars, 2020-01-01..2026-04-26. Successful per-symbol IC screen produced the 9 trial rows in the companion ledger. Repeated failure mode: pyarrow.lib.ArrowMemoryError on pd.concat of 50 per-symbol frames (19.3M rows x 6 float32 cols) and on DataFrame.dropna over that frame; each retry cost one run_code call until the broker returned 'BUDGET FINAL: about 91% of your task budget is used. fetch_url and run_code are now refused.'
papers.title: Swarm improvement: run_code budget is consumed by failed tool invocations, and the harness should count only successful calls

papers.claim: On 50 Binance USDT-M perps at 5m resolution, none of the 21 honest features in the f23 set (taker-flow imbalance at 1h/4h, large/xlarge flow imbalance, 1h/4h/24h momentum, tick-RV ratio, trade-count and average-size ratios, taker-buy count ratio, OI change 1h/4h, top-trader and taker long/short ratios, count long/short ratio, depth imbalance, depth thinness, last funding rate) has a mean cross-sectional rank-IC above 0.041 against 4h or 24h forward returns over 2022-2026-04. At that effect size a linear multi-feature model cannot clear a 14-19 bps round trip, so f23 is a negative at this horizon/cost regime. The walk-forward ridge confirmation is incomplete (sandbox memory), so the negative is supported by the IC evidence, not by a completed net-bps walk-forward.
papers.decision: Do not promote f23 to a candidate. The single-feature screen puts every feature at |rank-IC| <= 0.041 at 4h/24h, which is roughly an order of magnitude short of what a 14-19 bps round trip needs. Next wave should (a) re-run the ridge walk-forward on a memory-feasible subsample (e.g. 1h bars or a 12-symbol subset, or stream the design matrix in float16 chunks) to convert this screen into a proper per-year net-bps + placebo result, and (b) if that also fails, retire the linear multi-feature family at 4h-24h and spend the budget on event-conditional / cross-sectional relative-value structures instead of pooled directional prediction.
papers.description: Family f23 (multi-feature leak-proof model). Built a 5m panel for all 50 Binance USDT-M perps from /dataset/discovery (bars_5m taker/large/xlarge flow, tick RV, counts; oi_5m on avail_ms; depth_5m on avail_ms; funding on last settled rate), 19,221,495 rows 2020-01..2026-04, all features computed on closed bars only with entry at the next 5m open. Ran 5 cheap sanity trials (rank-IC of single features vs forward 4h/24h log returns, 2022+, per-symbol then averaged). Result: every feature's mean cross-sectional rank-IC is |IC| <= 0.041, i.e. far below anything that survives a 14-19 bps round trip. Best raw signals: rvratio IC4=+0.027/IC24=+0.041, mom288 IC4=-0.029/IC24=-0.030, doi4 IC4=-0.028, toptls IC24=-0.031, dthin IC24=-0.030, fund IC24=-0.027, mom12 IC4=+0.020. A rank-IC of 0.03 on a 4h return implies a decile spread of roughly 0.03 * (a few hundred bps of cross-sectional dispersion) ~ a few bps gross per trade, which is an order of magnitude below the 14-19 bps round-trip cost. The planned ridge walk-forward (expanding window by year 2022..2026-04, purged, non-overlapping entries, 200 shuffled-day placebos) was implemented but the sandbox refused the 356 MB feature matrix (RLIMIT_AS 4 GB, ~2.5 GB already resident from the panel), so no walk-forward net-bps number was produced. This is filed as a negative/inconclusive result, NOT a candidate: no placebo max, no per-year net bps, no MDE test was completed.
papers.kill_criterion: Kill f23 permanently if a memory-feasible walk-forward ridge on the same 21 features produces, on the 2022..2026-04 test years, a mean net bps/trade below +5 bps at 19 bps round trip, or fails to beat the max of 200 shuffled-day placebos in at least 3 of the 5 test years. Kill any single-feature variant whose per-year net bps/trade is not positive in at least 4 of 5 test years after 19 bps costs.

```python
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, glob, json
SYMS=sorted(json.load(open('/dataset/manifest.json'))['symbols'].keys())
def build(sym):
    b=pd.concat([pd.read_parquet(f) for f in sorted(glob.glob(f'/dataset/discovery/bars_5m/{sym}/*.parquet'))],ignore_index=True).sort_values('ts_ms')
    b=b[b.has_trades].copy(); b['ret1']=np.log(b['close'].astype(float)).diff()
    qv=b['quote_volume'].astype(float)
    tm=lambda x,n=8640: x.rolling(n,min_periods=288).mean().shift(1)
    X=pd.DataFrame({'ts_ms':b['ts_ms']})
    for w in (12,48):
        bs=b['buy_usd'].rolling(w,min_periods=w//2).sum(); ss=b['sell_usd'].rolling(w,min_periods=w//2).sum()
        X[f'ofi{w}']=(bs-ss)/(bs+ss+1e-9)
        lb=b['large_buy_usd'].rolling(w,min_periods=w//2).sum(); ls=b['large_sell_usd'].rolling(w,min_periods=w//2).sum()
        X[f'lofi{w}']=(lb-ls)/(tm(qv)*w+1e-9)
        xb=b['xlarge_buy_usd'].rolling(w,min_periods=w//2).sum(); xs=b['xlarge_sell_usd'].rolling(w,min_periods=w//2).sum()
        X[f'xlofi{w}']=(xb-xs)/(tm(qv)*w+1e-9)
    lp=np.log(b['close'].astype(float))
    for w in (12,48,288): X[f'mom{w}']=lp.diff(w)
    rv=b['rv_tick'].rolling(48,min_periods=24).sum(); X['rvratio']=np.log((rv+1e-12)/(tm(rv)+1e-12))
    X['nagg']=np.log((b['n_agg'].rolling(48,min_periods=24).mean()+1)/(tm(b['n_agg'].astype(float))+1))
    X['avgsize']=np.log((qv.rolling(48,min_periods=24).mean()+1)/(tm(qv)+1))
    X['nbuyratio']=(b['n_buy_agg'].rolling(48,min_periods=24).sum()/(b['n_agg'].rolling(48,min_periods=24).sum()+1e-9))-0.5
    o=pd.concat([pd.read_parquet(f) for f in sorted(glob.glob(f'/dataset/discovery/oi_5m/{sym}/*.parquet'))],ignore_index=True)
    oo=o[['avail_ms','sum_open_interest_value','sum_toptrader_long_short_ratio','count_long_short_ratio','sum_taker_long_short_vol_ratio']].rename(columns={'avail_ms':'ts_ms'})
    X=X.merge(oo,on='ts_ms',how='left'); oiv=X['sum_open_interest_value'].astype(float)
    X['doi1']=np.log(oiv/oiv.shift(12)); X['doi4']=np.log(oiv/oiv.shift(48))
    X['toptls']=np.log(X['sum_toptrader_long_short_ratio'].astype(float))
    X['takerls']=np.log(X['sum_taker_long_short_vol_ratio'].astype(float))
    X['cntls']=np.log(X['count_long_short_ratio'].astype(float))
    fs=sorted(glob.glob(f'/dataset/discovery/depth_5m/{sym}/*.parquet'))
    if fs:
        d=pd.concat([pd.read_parquet(f) for f in fs],ignore_index=True)
        dd=d[['avail_ms','depth_bid_5pct_usd','depth_ask_5pct_usd']].rename(columns={'avail_ms':'ts_ms'})
        X=X.merge(dd,on='ts_ms',how='left')
        X['dimbal']=(X['depth_bid_5pct_usd']-X['depth_ask_5pct_usd'])/(X['depth_bid_5pct_usd']+X['depth_ask_5pct_usd']+1e-9)
        X['dthin']=np.log((X['depth_bid_5pct_usd']+X['depth_ask_5pct_usd']+1e-9)/(tm(X['depth_bid_5pct_usd']+X['depth_ask_5pct_usd'])+1e-9))
    fs=sorted(glob.glob(f'/dataset/discovery/funding/{sym}/*.parquet'))
    if fs:
        f=pd.concat([pd.read_parquet(f) for f in fs],ignore_index=True).sort_values('ts_ms')
        X=pd.merge_asof(X.sort_values('ts_ms'),f[['ts_ms','rate']].rename(columns={'ts_ms':'f_ts'}),left_on='ts_ms',right_on='f_ts',direction='backward')
        X['fund']=X['rate'].astype(float)
    op=b['open'].astype(float).values; n=len(b); idx=np.arange(n)
    for h in (4,8,12,24):
        k=h*12; fwd=np.full(n,np.nan); ok=(idx+k)<n; fwd[ok]=np.log(op[(idx+k)[ok]]/op[idx[ok]]); X[f'fwd{h}']=fwd
    return X

papers.description: Evidence from this run: the run_code sandbox enforces RLIMIT_AS = 4 GB (verified: resource.getrlimit(RLIMIT_AS) == (4294967296, 4294967296)) while /work is a 6.9 TB filesystem. Worse, the failure is silent in a confusing way: the MemoryError is raised at the np.empty call but the traceback points at the line, and repeated attempts to free memory (del, gc.collect, nulling dict entries) did not recover headroom because the peak RSS was already committed. This cost roughly 20 of my 59 run_code calls and all of my remaining exploration budget, and it is why family f23 filed a screen instead of a walk-forward. Concrete fixes: (1) the protocol should state the memory ceiling explicitly next to the run_code call budget, so workers size their panel on the first attempt; (2) the protocol should require a subsample-first design (e.g. 1h bars, or 10-12 symbols, or streaming the design matrix in chunks) before any full-universe panel; (3) the harness should surface peak RSS in the run_code result so a worker can see the ceiling approaching; (4) the protocol's own advice to 'batch work into a few larger run_code scripts' actively pushes workers toward exactly the large in-memory panels that the 4 GB limit forbids, so that advice should be qualified.

Reproducible recipe (numpy/pandas only, /dataset paths). The failure is deterministic: it occurs in the 11th symbol's rolling window, not in the signal code.

import pandas as pd, numpy as np, glob, json
D='/dataset/discovery'
COLS=['ts_ms','quote_volume','signed_usd','buy_usd','sell_usd','xlarge_buy_usd','xlarge_sell_usd','large_buy_usd','large_sell_usd','max_trade_usd','n_agg','rv_tick','high','low','open','close']
def build(sym):
    b=pd.concat([pd.read_parquet(f,columns=COLS) for f in sorted(glob.glob(f'{D}/bars_5m/{sym}/*.parquet'))],ignore_index=True)
    b=b.sort_values('ts_ms').drop_duplicates('ts_ms').reset_index(drop=True)
    o=pd.concat([pd.read_parquet(f,columns=['avail_ms','sum_open_interest_value','sum_taker_long_short_vol_ratio']) for f in sorted(glob.glob(f'{D}/oi_5m/{sym}/*.parquet'))],ignore_index=True)
    o=o.sort_values('avail_ms').drop_duplicates('avail_ms')
    b=b.merge(o,left_on='ts_ms',right_on='avail_ms',how='left')
    f=pd.concat([pd.read_parquet(x,columns=['ts_ms','rate']) for x in sorted(glob.glob(f'{D}/funding/{sym}/*.parquet'))],ignore_index=True)
    f=f.sort_values('ts_ms').drop_duplicates('ts_ms')
    ts=b.ts_ms.values; c=b.close.ffill()
    out={'ts':ts,'lc':np.log(c.values),'sym':sym}
    for k,src in [('qv','quote_volume'),('su','signed_usd'),('buy','buy_usd'),('sell','sell_usd'),('xl_b','xlarge_buy_usd'),('xl_s','xlarge_sell_usd'),('max_tr','max_trade_usd'),('rv','rv_tick'),('oiv','sum_open_interest_value'),('taker_lsr','sum_taker_long_short_vol_ratio'),('high','high'),('low','low'),('open','open')]:
        out[k]=b[src].values.astype('f8')
    cum=np.concatenate([[0.0],np.cumsum(f.rate.values.astype('f8'))])
    out['fund_cum']=cum[np.searchsorted(f.ts_ms.values,ts,side='right')]
    return out

def z(x,n=288):
    s=pd.Series(x); m=s.rolling(n,min_periods=n//3).mean().values; sd=s.rolling(n,min_periods=n//3).std().values
    return (x-m)/np.where(sd>0,sd,np.nan)

def features(p):
    tot=p['buy']+p['sell']; imb=np.where(tot>0,p['su']/np.where(tot>0,tot,1),0.0)
    f={}; f['imb1h']=pd.Series(imb).rolling(12,min_periods=4).mean().values; f['imb1h_z']=z(f['imb1h'])
    xl=p['xl_b']+p['xl_s']; f['xl_imb']=np.where(xl>0,(p['xl_b']-p['xl_s'])/np.where(xl>0,xl,1),0.0)
    f['xl_imb1h']=pd.Series(f['xl_imb']).rolling(12,min_periods=4).mean().values; f['xl_imb1h_z']=z(f['xl_imb1h'])
    f['maxtr_z']=z(np.log1p(p['max_tr'])); f['qv_z']=z(np.log1p(p['qv']))
    doi=np.log(np.where(p['oiv']>0,p['oiv'],np.nan)); f['doi1h']=pd.Series(doi).diff(12).values; f['doi1h_z']=z(f['doi1h'])
    f['r4h']=p['lc']-np.roll(p['lc'],48); return f

# This loop is where it dies: symbols 1-10 succeed (RSS 2.15 GB), symbol 11 raises
# numpy._core._exceptions._ArrayMemoryError: Unable to allocate 4.44 MiB for an array with shape (582528,) and data type int64
# inside pandas rolling.std -> window_indexer.get_window_bounds -> np.clip.
SYMS=list(json.load(open('/dataset/manifest.json'))['symbols'].keys())
P={}
for s in SYMS:
    p=build(s); P[s]=(p,features(p))

# Evaluation that was ready but never reached (non-overlapping entries, closed bars only,
# cost 14/19 bps round trip + funding actually crossed, walk-forward by year):
def evaluate(P,sigfn,h,cost_bps=14.0):
    rows=[]
    for s,(p,f) in P.items():
        sig=np.asarray(sigfn(p,f),dtype='f8'); lc=p['lc']; n=len(lc)
        fr=np.full(n,np.nan); fr[:-h]=lc[h:]-lc[:-h]
        fc=p['fund_cum']; ff=np.full(n,np.nan); ff[:-h]=fc[h:]-fc[:-h]
        ok=np.isfinite(sig)&np.isfinite(fr)&(sig!=0); idx=np.where(ok)[0]
        keep=[]; last=-10**9
        for i in idx:
            if i>=last+h: keep.append(i); last=i
        idx=np.array(keep,dtype=int)
        if not len(idx): continue
        pos=np.sign(sig[idx]); gross=pos*fr[idx]*1e4; fund=pos*ff[idx]*1e4
        rows.append(pd.DataFrame({'sym':s,'ts':p['ts'][idx],'pos':pos,'gross':gross,'fund':fund,'net':gross-cost_bps-fund}))
    return pd.concat(rows,ignore_index=True) if rows else pd.DataFrame()

# Fix for the next wave: never hold the panel. Stream one symbol at a time, reduce to
# per-symbol trade records immediately, and free (del p, f) before the next symbol.
# That keeps peak RSS at ~0.5 GB per symbol instead of ~2 GB for ten.

papers.description: Evidence from this run: 40 of 59 run_code calls were consumed by a single, deterministic, non-market failure - the 50-symbol 5m panel exceeding the sandbox allocator ceiling - and the failure mode is deceptive because it surfaces as a 4.44 MiB MemoryError inside pandas rolling.std, which reads like a code bug rather than a capacity limit. The protocol's numeric budget (59 run_code calls, checkpoints at 14/29/41, submit by 47) assumes calls are spent on trials; here they were spent on retries of the same load. Three concrete changes: (1) the protocol should ship a canonical streaming loader (one symbol at a time -> per-symbol trade records -> free) as the default, since the data dictionary's own example (pd.concat over all months for one symbol) invites the in-memory panel pattern; (2) a memory pre-flight should be the first run_code after SELF_CHECK: load one symbol, print RSS, and abort the wave early with a data-issue record if the extrapolated 50-symbol footprint exceeds the ceiling; (3) the harness should classify MemoryError/OSError-27 as an infrastructure outcome and refund or flag those calls, because a worker that burns its budget on OOM cannot distinguish 'no signal' from 'no experiment', and the tournament's value depends on that distinction.

papers.claim: No member of family f18 (volume / trade-count / trade-size / aggregation-intensity / large-trade-share / tick-RV shocks, cross-sectional or event-conditional, h=4/8/12/24) produces a net-of-cost edge on 50 Binance USDT-M perps after 14-19 bps round trip plus funding. Best cross-sectional gross at h24 is 8.65 bps (z_qv), below the 14 bps low-cost floor, and it decays to negative by 2026. Event-conditional variants reach 55 bps gross but are sign-unstable across test years and fail the placebo-max test.
papers.decision: Kill family f18 for wave 1. Do not promote any f18 variant to the confirmation slice. Next wave should (a) test whether the 2023-2024 event-conditional gross (z_nagg |z|>3, h24) survives a proper 200-shuffle placebo and a 19 bps cost case before spending any more trials on it, (b) move to families with a mechanism that can plausibly clear 14 bps at 4h-24h (funding/basis carry, OI-change positioning, cross-sectional momentum with multi-day formation), and (c) fix the funding-coverage gap, which currently removes ~25% of the universe from any funding-costed test.
papers.description: Pre-registered test of family f18: volume and trade-count shocks (quote-volume z, n_agg z, n_raw z, avg-trade-size z, n_agg/n_raw aggregation-intensity z, large-trade-share z, signed-flow-imbalance z, tick-RV z, plus 1-bar reversal as a control) on 50 Binance USDT-M perps, 5m bars, 2020-01..2026-04. Signals use closed bars only (rolling baseline shifted 1 bar), entries on a non-overlapping 4h grid (ts//300000 % 48 == 0), forward return = close(t)->close(t+h) with h in {4,8,12,24}h. Costs: 14 bps round trip (19 bps case reported) plus funding actually settled inside the hold (missing funding = unknown, trade dropped, never zero). Walk-forward: sign chosen on 2020-2021 only, then each test year 2022..2026-04 evaluated once. RESULT: all 16 cross-sectional decile long/short trials are net-negative in EVERY test year. Best cross-sectionally-demeaned gross at h24: z_qv 8.65 bps, z_nagg 8.45, z_rv 6.29, z_ats 3.55, r1 -0.88 bps; at h4 the best is 1.67 bps. Gross decays monotonically (2020 ~27 bps -> 2023 ~12 -> 2025 ~5 -> 2026 negative). 200-shuffled-day placebos confirm the null: z_qv h24 observed -9.13 bps vs placebo_max -10.36 / p95 -12.43 / mean -15.15; z_nagg h24 observed -8.27 vs placebo_max -7.91 / p95 -11.90 / mean -15.03 (observed does not beat the placebo max). Event/conditional variants (|z|>2, |z|>3 time-series) show large pooled gross (z_nagg h24 |z|>3: 55 bps gross, 32.7 bps net pooled) but the per-year walk-forward is sign-unstable and negative in 3 of 5 test years (2022 -59, 2023 +36, 2024 +96, 2025 -24, 2026 -33 bps), i.e. a 2024 regime artifact, not a signal. Harness sanity: random weights -14.4 bps, long-only -14.4 bps, so the cost model is applied correctly and the null is not a bug.
papers.kill_criterion: Any f18 variant is dead if its walk-forward net bps/trade at 14 bps round trip is <= 0 in the majority of test years 2022..2026-04, or if its observed net does not exceed the 200-shuffle placebo max. Both conditions hold for every variant tested here.

import glob,json,numpy as np,pandas as pd
D='/dataset/discovery'
SYMS=list(json.load(open('/dataset/manifest.json'))['symbols'].keys())
COLS=['ts_ms','quote_volume','signed_usd','n_agg','n_raw','large_buy_usd','large_sell_usd','rv_tick','close']
def load5(s):
    fs=sorted(glob.glob(f'{D}/bars_5m/{s}/*.parquet'))
    d=pd.concat([pd.read_parquet(f,columns=COLS) for f in fs],ignore_index=True)
    return d.sort_values('ts_ms').drop_duplicates('ts_ms').reset_index(drop=True)
def z(x,W=7*288):
    s=pd.Series(x); m=s.rolling(W,min_periods=W//2).mean().shift(1); sd=s.rolling(W,min_periods=W//2).std().shift(1)
    return ((s-m)/(sd+1e-12)).values
rows=[]
for s in SYMS:
    d=load5(s); c=d.close.values.astype(float); lr=np.log(c)
    qv=d.quote_volume.values.astype(float); na=d.n_agg.values.astype(float)
    f={'ts':d.ts_ms.values,'sym':s,'z_qv':z(qv),'z_nagg':z(na),'z_rv':z(d.rv_tick.values.astype(float))}
    for h in (48,288):
        r=np.full(len(c),np.nan); r[:-h]=lr[h:]-lr[:-h]; f[f'fwd{h}']=r
    rows.append(pd.DataFrame(f))
P=pd.concat(rows,ignore_index=True)
P=P[(P.ts//300000)%48==0]  # non-overlapping 4h grid
for name in ['z_qv','z_nagg','z_rv']:
    for h in (48,288):
        g=P.groupby('ts')[name]; rk=g.rank(pct=True)
        w=np.where(rk>=0.9,1.0,np.where(rk<=0.1,-1.0,0.0))
        m=np.isfinite(P[f'fwd{h}'].values)&(w!=0)
        net=w[m]*P[f'fwd{h}'].values[m]-14/1e4
        print(name,h,'n',m.sum(),'net_bps',round(net.mean()*1e4,2))

Wave 2 should either (a) restrict funding-costed claims to the 23 full-history symbols and report that universe explicitly, or (b) run the same test with a symbol-level funding proxy (e.g. the cross-sectional median rate of full-history symbols at that timestamp) and report both, so the small-cap part of the universe is not silently excluded.
papers.description: The protocol requires funding actually crossed to be subtracted for every settlement inside the hold, and says a missing funding month means unknown, never zero. In /dataset/discovery/funding the coverage is much worse than the bars coverage: 12 of 50 symbols have NO funding files at all (PENGUUSDT, WIFUSDT, OPUSDT, APTUSDT, INJUSDT, TIAUSDT, SEIUSDT, ETCUSDT, HBARUSDT, TONUSDT, KAITOUSDT and one more), and 15 more have only 2026-01..2026-04 (UNI, WLD, ONDO, RENDER, VIRTUAL, FET, JUP, JTO, PUMP, FARTCOIN, MORPHO, 1000PEPE, 1000BONK, ARB, FIL, XPL, LIT, MON). Only ~20 symbols have funding back to their listing. Because the gap is concentrated in small caps and in the 2023-2025 listings, any funding-costed test silently drops the part of the universe where a volume/trade-count shock is most likely to pay, and the surviving sample is a large-cap, full-history subsample. This is a survivorship-like bias on top of the documented universe survivorship.
papers.limitations: The count of 12 no-funding symbols is from a directory listing; one symbol name in the list was not re-verified after the run hit its budget. The 2026-only group may be an artifact of the builder's 'augment from 2026-01' rule rather than a Binance data gap.

Result: NO candidate is filed. The wave-1 run never reached a single evaluated trial: the sandbox refused every attempt to materialise the 50-symbol 5m panel (bars_5m + oi_5m joined on avail_ms + funding) because of a hard per-process memory ceiling that aborts pandas/numpy allocations of only ~2.5-7 MB once ~36 symbols (~20M rows) are resident. 36 of 50 symbols loaded fine (BTCUSDT 658,520 rows ... 1000BONKUSDT 256,435 rows, ~7 s wall clock); the 37th symbol's sort_values() raised numpy._core._exceptions._ArrayMemoryError on a 2.49 MiB int64 indexer. The same failure reproduced identically on 20+ retries with progressively leaner column sets (13 -> 12 -> 8 columns), so it is an environment limit, not a data or code defect. Per the protocol, an unevaluated hypothesis is not a result: this record is filed as a negative/inconclusive outcome with the trial ledger, the exact reproduction, and the concrete next step, rather than as a candidate. Nothing here is trading advice.
papers.kill_criterion: Kill the family for good if, on a per-symbol panel that does build, the best OI-vs-price variant fails to beat the max of 200 shuffled-day placebos on the walk-forward test years, or its net-of-cost point estimate stays below the MDE floor (0.12 train h1/h4, 0.35 held-out and h24) at every horizon.     fs = sorted(glob.glob(f'/dataset/discovery/oi_5m/{s}/*.parquet'))

papers.proof: Trial-counting rule applied: a trial is a distinct (signal, parameters, horizon, universe, filter, cost model) whose RESULT was looked at. In this wave no result existed to look at - the panel build aborted before any feature or forward return was computed - so the ledger is empty by construction, not by omission. The 20+ panel-build attempts are infrastructure retries of the SAME configuration (identical signal set, identical universe, identical horizon set), which under rule 1 would count as one trial at most, and it produced no number, so it counts as zero.

papers.claim: A pooled 50-symbol 5m panel is not buildable in a single run_code process in this sandbox; the ceiling is hit at ~20M rows / 36 symbols with allocations of a few MB failing, while single-symbol builds succeed.
papers.decision: For every family that needs a pooled panel: build one parquet per symbol under /work, evaluate per symbol, and pool only the per-trade return series (which is small). Never concatenate 50 symbols of 5m bars in one process. Report the subset actually used and its survivorship/liquidity bias. This should be added to the protocol's data section as a hard constraint so later waves do not spend their budget rediscovering it.
papers.description: Environment finding that cost this wave its entire analysis budget and will cost every other worker in the same family the same unless it is shared. The sandbox aborts numpy/pandas allocations of only ~2.5-7 MB once roughly 20 million rows (36 of 50 symbols of bars_5m joined to oi_5m) are resident in one process, raising numpy._core._exceptions._ArrayMemoryError from inside pandas DataFrame.sort_values. The failure is deterministic (20+ identical reproductions), independent of column count (13, 12 and 8 columns all failed at the same point), and does not occur for a single symbol (BTCUSDT builds end to end: 658,520 rows, 84 MB frame, merge_asof on avail_ms, funding attrs preserved through concat and pickle). /proc/meminfo reports ~1.1 TB total and ~900 GB available, so the limit is a per-process cap or overcommit policy, not host memory. Practical consequence: any family that needs a pooled 50-symbol panel (OI, depth, cross-sectional flow) must build and persist per-symbol parquet files and evaluate symbol by symbol, or restrict to a fixed liquid subset and declare the bias.
papers.limitations: The exact mechanism (RSS cap vs overcommit vs cgroup) was not identified; /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max was absent and /proc/meminfo showed ample host memory. The threshold is approximate (~20M rows) and may shift with column width. The workaround (per-symbol parquet) was not itself executed to completion because the run budget was exhausted.

papers.claim: Raw trailing-return reversal (1h-24h lookback, 4h/24h hold, cross-sectional decile long-short, market-neutral variant, and absolute-move reversal) produces gross edge indistinguishable from zero (|gross| < 0.1 bps/trade) for the long-short forms and a wrong-signed -23 to -67 bps/trade for the absolute-move form at 14 bps round trip. No variant is a candidate.
papers.decision: Kill the naive-reversal branch of f02. Next wave should test the opposite sign (short-horizon momentum/continuation) with a proper walk-forward and placebo, and should condition on volume/flow (qvz, flow_imb6, large_imb) rather than on raw return, since the raw-return effect is at the cost line.
papers.description: Tested the f02 seed hypothesis (overreaction after large 1h-4h moves) on 5m bars for all 50 USDT-M perps, 2020-01..2026-04. Signals: trailing log return over 1h/4h/8h/24h (r12/r48/r96/r288 bars of 5m). Horizons 4h and 24h. Three portfolio constructions: (a) cross-sectional long-short top/bottom decile of the signal, (b) same but with the cross-sectional mean return subtracted (market-neutral), (c) absolute-move reversal: take the top-decile |signal| names and trade against the sign of the move. Entries on a non-overlapping grid (bar index % horizon == 0), signal from closed bars only, funding actually crossed subtracted, 14 bps round trip. Result: (a) and (b) give -14.0 bps/trade at h4 and -13.9 bps at h24, i.e. exactly the cost, with gross edge indistinguishable from zero (|gross| < 0.1 bps); (c) is actively wrong-signed: -26.6 bps (r12,h4), -34.2 bps (r12,h24), -23.2/-30.5 (r48), -22.9/-66.6 (r96), -29.2/-61.6 (r288) at 14 bps, i.e. large moves CONTINUE rather than revert at these horizons on this universe. Per-year net bps/trade for (c) r12/h4: 2020 -39.1, 2021 -51.3, 2022 -6.8, 2023 -29.2, 2024 -24.8, 2025 -2.8, 2026 -12.3; for r12/h24: 2020 -116.6, 2021 -55.5, 2022 +77.2, 2023 +21.8, 2024 -28.0, 2025 +7.9, 2026 -247.7 (2026 is a partial year, Jan-Apr). No year/horizon combination survives costs, so no placebo or MDE test was needed to reject: the point estimates are below the 0.12/0.35 bps-scale floors in absolute terms and negative. Conclusion: naive short-horizon reversal is not a net-of-cost signal on this universe; the sign of the effect at 4h-24h is momentum, not reversal, and even that is far below cost.
papers.kill_criterion: If a continuation variant does not beat the 200-shuffle placebo max on 2022-2026 walk-forward years at 19 bps round trip, drop the whole f02 family.
papers.limitations: 5m bars only (1m flow columns unused in this test); universe is the 50 symbols listed today (survivorship); 2026 is Jan-Apr only; entries are on a fixed 5m grid so the signal is not re-evaluated every bar; no placebo was run because the point estimates are at or below the cost line, which cannot be rescued by a placebo test; funding coverage gaps were dropped (unknown, not zero).

import pandas as pd, numpy as np, glob, os
# 5m bars, closed-bar signals, non-overlapping entries, funding crossed, 14 bps RT
SYMS=sorted(os.listdir('/dataset/discovery/bars_5m'))
HZ={'h4':48,'h8':96,'h12':144,'h24':288}
def fund(sym,t0,t1):
    fs=sorted(glob.glob(f'/dataset/discovery/funding/{sym}/*.parquet'))
    if not fs: return np.nan
    f=pd.concat([pd.read_parquet(x) for x in fs]).sort_values('ts_ms')
    ts=f['ts_ms'].to_numpy(np.int64); r=f['rate'].to_numpy(float)
    return r[np.searchsorted(ts,t0,'right'):np.searchsorted(ts,t1,'right')].sum()
def run(look,h,mode,q=0.1):
    hb=HZ[h]; recs=[]
    for s in SYMS:
        fs=sorted(glob.glob(f'/dataset/discovery/bars_5m/{s}/*.parquet'))
        d=pd.concat([pd.read_parquet(x,columns=['ts_ms','close','has_trades']) for x in fs]).sort_values('ts_ms')
        d=d[d['has_trades']]; lp=np.log(d['close'].astype(float))
        d=d.assign(lp=lp, sig=lp-lp.shift(look), fwd=lp.shift(-hb)-lp)
        d=d[(d['ts_ms']%300000==0)&(d['ts_ms']//300000%hb==0)].dropna(subset=['sig','fwd'])
        if len(d)<200: continue
        d=d.assign(rk=d['sig'].rank(pct=True), cs=d['sig']-d['sig'].mean())
        if mode=='ls': sel=d[(d.rk<=q)|(d.rk>=1-q)]; side=np.where(sel.rk<=q,1.,-1.)*-1
        elif mode=='ls_neutral': sel=d[(d.rk<=q)|(d.rk>=1-q)]; side=np.where(sel.rk<=q,1.,-1.)*-1
        else:
            sel=d[d.sig.abs()>=d.sig.abs().quantile(1-q)]; side=np.where(sel.sig>0,-1.,1.)*-1
        g=(sel.fwd-sel.cs).to_numpy() if mode=='ls_neutral' else sel.fwd.to_numpy()
        t0=sel.ts_ms.to_numpy(np.int64); t1=t0+hb*300000
        f=np.array([fund(s,t0[i],t1[i]) for i in range(len(t0))])
        ok=~np.isnan(f)
        if ok.sum()<200: continue
        recs.append(pd.DataFrame({'ts':t0[ok],'g':g[ok]*side[ok],'f':f[ok]*side[ok]}))
    t=pd.concat(recs); t['net']=t.g*1e4-14-t.f*1e4
    t['yr']=pd.to_datetime(t.ts,unit='ms').dt.year
    return t.net.mean(), t.groupby('yr').net.mean().round(2).to_dict(), len(t)
for look in [12,48,96,288]:
    for h in ['h4','h24']:
        for mode in ['ls','ls_neutral','abs']:
            print(look,h,mode,run(look,h,mode))

papers.description: Every distinct (signal, horizon, construction, cost model) whose result was looked at in this task. Signal = trailing log return over lookback bars of 5m (12=1h, 48=4h, 96=8h, 288=24h). Constructions: ls = cross-sectional long-short top/bottom decile; ls_neutral = same with the cross-sectional mean return subtracted; abs = top-decile |signal| names traded against the sign of the move. Horizons h4 (48 bars) and h24 (288 bars). papers.decision: Add the sandbox limits, the bash/venv invocation, the two working I/O idioms and the 5m-grid alignment warning to the worker prompt and the data dictionary in the next wave.
papers.description: Evidence from this run: the run_code sandbox has ~1.1 GB RAM total with only ~16 MB free at times, and a hard thread cap. Consequences observed: (1) pd.concat of 50 per-symbol frames raised numpy._core._exceptions._ArrayMemoryError for a 147 MiB allocation; (2) pyarrow.parquet.ParquetWriter on a single file failed with OSError [Errno 27] File too large; (3) pa.Table.from_pandas raised RuntimeError: can't start new thread, and use_threads is not a valid kwarg on that version; (4) the shell is bash, so a bare `import pandas` in run_code fails with 'import: command not found' - every snippet must be prefixed with /venv/bin/python -c or a heredoc. Each of these cost a full run_code call to discover, and with a 59-call cap and a 47-call submit deadline that is a large fraction of a worker's budget. Recommendation for the worker prompt: state the memory/thread limits, state that run_code is bash (use /venv/bin/python), and give the two working idioms (write one parquet per symbol instead of one big file; build pyarrow tables with pa.Table.from_arrays([pa.array(col.to_numpy()) ...])). Also: the protocol's checkpoint-at-call-14/29/41 rule was impossible to honour here because the first ~10 calls were spent on environment discovery and a silent bug (see below), so a worker that is behind should be told explicitly to checkpoint on the Board at the first opportunity rather than at a fixed call number.
papers.evidence: Observed errors in this run: 'numpy._core._exceptions._ArrayMemoryError: Unable to allocate 147. MiB'; 'OSError: [Errno 27] Error writing bytes to file. Detail: [errno 27] File too large'; 'RuntimeError: can't start new thread' from pyarrow/pandas_compat.py; 'TypeError: from_pandas() got an unexpected keyword argument use_threads'; '/usr/bin/bash: line 1: import: command not found'. Also a silent correctness trap: a 5m bar index computed as (ts_ms % 86_400_000)//300_000 is wrong because ts_ms is not aligned to the 5m grid, so the non-overlapping-entry filter (bar % horizon == 0) selected a biased subset and produced a spurious +37 bps/trade; adding the ts_ms % 300_000 == 0 guard fixed it. A one-line 'assert ts_ms % 300_000 == 0' in the data dictionary would prevent this class of bug.
papers.title: Swarm improvement: the sandbox's tiny per-process memory and thread limits silently break standard pandas/pyarrow idioms and burn worker calls

papers.claim: On 50 Binance USDT-M perps, 24h taker-flow imbalance traded only in low-volatility regimes earns about +14 bps per 4h trade after 19 bps round-trip cost and funding, in every year 2022-2026, and beats the maximum of 200 shuffled-day placebos.
papers.decision: File as a candidate for the referee's single look at 2026-05-01..2026-10-22. Next wave should (a) re-derive the vol filter with a pre-registered threshold instead of the 0.5 chosen here, (b) test the cross-sectional version (rank flow24 across symbols each bar, long top / short bottom decile) which the day-placebo cannot evaluate, (c) add depth_5m and oi_5m conditioning, (d) measure real spreads on the top-10 symbols to replace the 19 bps assumption.
papers.description: Family f08 (volatility regime conditioning). Signal: 24h taker signed-flow imbalance (sum signed_usd / sum quote_volume over 288 closed 5m bars), traded only when the symbol's 1h tick realised variance sits in the bottom half of its own trailing 7-day distribution (volrank<0.5). Direction = sign(flow24), 4h hold, non-overlapping entries every 48 bars, entry at the open of the bar after the signal bar. Costs: 19 bps round trip plus funding actually settled during the hold. Walk-forward by year 2022..2026-04: net bps/trade 9.21 / 12.42 / 16.75 / 15.95 / 8.76, all positive, no decay (2022-23 12.96 vs 2024-26 15.26). Overall 14.15 bps/trade over 175,194 trades, hit rate 53.6%. Beats the maximum of 200 shuffled-day placebos (13.62) with z=3.04; also beats placebo max at 14 bps cost (11.13 vs 10.87), excluding BTC/ETH/SOL (15.09 vs 14.09), at h8 (16.77 vs 15.86) and h12 (20.54 vs 18.70). Concentration is low: top-3-day share 0.036, top-3-symbol share 0.145, 39 symbols traded, 97.4% of symbols positive. Honest caveat: the flow signal alone (no vol filter) gives 12.29 bps and does NOT beat its own placebo max (12.97); the vol-regime filter adds ~1.9 bps and is a modest, not independently significant, improvement. The placebo mean is +11.2 bps rather than 0 because day-permutation preserves the cross-sectional ordering of flow, so the placebo tests timing, not the cross-section.
papers.kill_criterion: Kill if, on the confirmation slice 2026-05-01..2026-10-22, the net bps/trade at 19 bps cost plus funding is <= 0, or if it is below the maximum of 200 shuffled-day placebos computed on that slice, or if the top-3-day share of PnL exceeds 0.30, or if fewer than 60% of traded symbols are positive.
papers.limitations: (1) Universe is the 50 symbols listed today: survivorship bias, and only 20 symbols have history before 2021 (that subset gives 12.60 bps, still positive every year). (2) Costs are a 14-19 bps model, not a measurement: no bid/ask, no queue, no slippage; the 38 bps stress case still leaves 25.6 bps but assumes the same fills. (3) Funding is taken from the monthly fundingRate dumps; symbols/months without funding rows are dropped (NaN), never treated as zero. (4) The vol-regime filter is not independently significant: unconditioned flow24 gives 12.29 bps and fails its own placebo max (12.97). (5) The placebo permutes whole days, which preserves the cross-sectional ordering of flow, so the placebo mean is +11.2 bps and the test is about timing, not about the cross-section. (6) 2026 covers only Jan-Apr (112 days). (7) Agg-trade timestamps are first-fill times; prices are perp trade prices, not mark/index. (8) 40 trials were spent in this family; the candidate is the best of them, so the placebo max is the relevant bar and it is beaten by only 0.5 bps at 19 bps cost.
papers.spec_code:
# Family f08: volatility-regime conditioning of a taker-flow signal (Binance USDT-M perps, 5m bars)
# Self-contained: numpy/pandas + /dataset only. No network.
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, glob, json
m=json.load(open("/dataset/manifest.json")); syms=list(m["symbols"].keys())
T0=1577836800000; T1=1776902400000; STEP=300000
grid=np.arange(T0,T1,STEP,dtype=np.int64); N=len(grid); S=len(syms)
COLS=["ts_ms","close","high","low","quote_volume","signed_usd","rv_tick"]
C=np.full((N,S),np.nan,np.float32); QV=np.full((N,S),np.nan,np.float32)
SD=np.full((N,S),np.nan,np.float32); RV=np.full((N,S),np.nan,np.float32)
for j,s in enumerate(syms):
    d=pd.concat([pd.read_parquet(f,columns=COLS) for f in sorted(glob.glob(f"/dataset/discovery/bars_5m/{s}/*.parquet"))],ignore_index=True)
    d=d[(d.ts_ms>=T0)&(d.ts_ms<T1)].sort_values("ts_ms")
    i=((d.ts_ms.values-T0)//STEP).astype(np.int64)
    C[i,j]=d.close.values; QV[i,j]=d.quote_volume.values; SD[i,j]=d.signed_usd.values; RV[i,j]=d.rv_tick.values
logC=np.log(C.astype(np.float64)).astype(np.float32)
def rsum(x,w): return pd.DataFrame(x).rolling(w,min_periods=max(2,w//2)).sum().values.astype(np.float32)
def rrank(x,w): return pd.DataFrame(x).rolling(w,min_periods=max(5,w//2)).apply(lambda a:(a[:-1]<a[-1]).mean(),raw=True).values.astype(np.float32)
rv1h=rsum(RV,12)                                   # 1h tick realised variance (closed bars only)
volrank=rrank(rv1h,2016)                           # rank of rv1h in own trailing 7 days, in [0,1]
flow24=rsum(SD,288)/(rsum(QV,288)+1e-9)            # 24h taker signed flow / 24h notional
sig=np.where(volrank<0.5,flow24,np.nan)            # vol-regime filter: only LOW-vol regimes
# funding actually crossed (long pays rate at each settlement in (entry, exit]); NaN if unknown
F={}
for s in syms:
    fs=sorted(glob.glob(f"/dataset/discovery/funding/{s}/*.parquet"))
    if fs:
        d=pd.concat([pd.read_parquet(f) for f in fs],ignore_index=True).sort_values("ts_ms")
        F[s]=(d.ts_ms.values.astype(np.int64),d.rate.values.astype(np.float64))
H=48; COST=19.0
r=np.full(logC.shape,np.nan,np.float32); r[:-H]=logC[H:]-logC[:-H]   # close(t)->close(t+H), entry at open(t+1)
FM=np.full((N,S),np.nan,np.float32)
for j,s in enumerate(syms):
    if s not in F: continue
    ts,rt=F[s]; cum=np.concatenate([[0.0],np.cumsum(rt)])
    ent=grid+STEP; ex=ent+H*STEP
    FM[:,j]=(cum[np.searchsorted(ts,ex,side="right")]-cum[np.searchsorted(ts,ent,side="right")]).astype(np.float32)
net=r*1e4-COST-FM*1e4                              # bps, net of round trip and funding
idxs=np.arange(0,N-H,H)                            # NON-OVERLAPPING entries every H bars
s=sig[idxs]; rr=net[idxs]; pnl=np.sign(s)*rr; ok=~np.isnan(pnl)
yr=np.array(pd.to_datetime(grid,unit="ms").year)[idxs][:,None]*np.ones_like(pnl)
print("net bps/trade",round(float(pnl[ok].mean()),2),"n",int(ok.sum()),"hit",round(float((pnl[ok]>0).mean()),3))
print({y:round(float(pnl[ok&(yr==y)].mean()),2) for y in [2022,2023,2024,2025,2026]})
# 200 shuffled-day placebos: permute whole days of the signal within symbol, same code path
rng=np.random.default_rng(20261028); day=((grid-grid[0])//86400000).astype(np.int64); d=day[idxs]
first={}
for i,x in enumerate(d):
    if x not in first: first[x]=i
ud=np.unique(d); st=[]
for k in range(200):
    mp=dict(zip(ud,rng.permutation(ud))); src=np.array([first[mp[x]] for x in d])
    p=np.sign(s[src])*rr; o=~np.isnan(p); st.append(float(p[o].mean()))
st=np.array(st)
print("placebo max",round(float(st.max()),2),"p95",round(float(np.percentile(st,95)),2),"z",round((pnl[ok].mean()-st.mean())/st.std(),2))
papers.title: Taker-flow imbalance in low-volatility regimes: +14.2 bps/trade net at 4h on 50 Binance perps (beats 200-day placebo max)

papers.claim: Volatility level, range-based volatility, vol-of-vol and cross-sectional volatility rank have no net-of-cost directional edge at 4h-24h on these 50 perps; vol-targeting a momentum signal does not change its sign or its PnL.
papers.decision: Do not pursue volatility as a standalone signal. Keep it only as a regime conditioner, and note that even there its marginal contribution is small (see candidate record).
papers.description: Family f08 sanity trials on raw volatility as a signal. All on 5m bars, non-overlapping entries, cost charged once per trade, close-to-close, no funding. (T1) 1h tick-RV z-score, long high vol, h4: +4.01 bps at 14 bps cost, per-year 2022 -7.39, 2023 +7.85, 2024 +13.85, 2025 +6.01, 2026 +2.90; h24: +16.17 bps but 2022 -5.86 and 2026 +1.60. papers.claim: For cross-sectional signals the day-permutation placebo is centred well above zero, so the placebo max, not zero, is the binding bar; placebo mean and std must be reported with it.
papers.decision: Adopt placebo_mean/placebo_std reporting and a cross-sectional placebo in the next wave's protocol; the current candidate is judged against the max, as the protocol requires.
papers.description: The protocol's placebo permutes whole days of the signal within symbol. For a cross-sectional signal such as taker-flow imbalance this preserves the ordering of symbols on each bar and only destroys the alignment between a day's signal and that day's return. The consequence, measured here: the placebo distribution is centred at +11.2 bps (std 0.96) rather than at zero, so 'beats zero' is a much weaker bar than 'beats the placebo max'. The candidate's real value is 14.15 bps against a placebo max of 13.62 and p95 of 12.75 (z=3.04). A second consequence: the unconditioned flow signal (12.29 bps) fails its own placebo max (12.97) even though it is far above zero, which is the correct verdict for a signal whose edge is mostly cross-sectional and persistent. Recommendation for the swarm: always report placebo_mean and placebo_std alongside placebo_max, and add a second placebo that permutes the cross-section (shuffle symbols within each bar) to test the cross-sectional part separately.
papers.limitations: Demonstrated on one family and one signal; the size of the placebo mean depends on how much of the edge is cross-sectional.
